LanguageData.ShuttleCargoBoardingHold: The shuttle is waiting for {0} to board before it departs.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLaunchDesc: Decides how shuttles sent by quests are loaded and when they leave the map. Changes take effect immediately; a flight already under way is not affected.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLoadingPanel: Quest shuttles always show the loading panel
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLoadingPanelTip:
When enabled, any shuttle the quest expects you to load (one that names a number of colonists to bring) always shows the vanilla loading panel: you can tick people and cargo, see the mass bar, and use the load, unload and cancel buttons.

Why this is needed: the load button and the panel both hang off the shuttle's current ship job. While a shuttle is parked on the map with an empty job queue - which is exactly what the Ideology "ancient complex" mission does, since the shuttle only queues its flights once you have finished loading - vanilla hides that whole row of buttons, so the panel cannot be opened at all and the only way in is to right-click each unit and send it aboard.

Shuttles the Empire handles by itself, such as the bestowing ceremony and the crashed shuttle rescue, are unaffected: those missions were never meant to let you put anything aboard.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoManualLaunch: Quest shuttles wait for a manual launch
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoManualLaunchTip:
When enabled, a quest shuttle no longer flies away just because every colonist the quest asked for is aboard. Instead it waits for you to press Launch, exactly like a permit shuttle.

Why this is needed: the vanilla "ready to leave" check only counts the colonists the quest asked for. It knows nothing about the mechanoids and ghouls this mod lets aboard, so the shuttle would take off while they were still walking to the hatch.

The Launch button appears in the shuttle's own button bar. It is greyed out while the colonist requirement is unmet, with the missing number spelled out. While a shuttle is parked with no ship job at all (the "ancient complex" mission right after landing, for example), this mod adds the same Launch button: pressing it asks the quest to re-check the load and depart the way the quest intended.

When disabled, vanilla behaviour returns: the shuttle departs as soon as the required things are loaded, and this mod still waits up to six hours for units that are still boarding. The quest's own countdown and its "leave if one of these units is lost" rules always apply unchanged.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitSection: Quest shuttle passenger and mass limits
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitDesc:
This section only covers shuttles a quest sends for you to load with your own colonists. Mass and passenger limits can be turned off independently.

On the return trip (loading on the mission map), prisoners never use a passenger slot, so you can bring captives home. If colonists die on the mission, the required headcount is capped at the free colonists still available, so the shuttle is not stuck forever waiting for a number that can no longer be met.

Royalty hospitality pickups are not covered.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoMassLimitEnabledTip: When unchecked, the loading panel no longer rejects an overloaded load. The mass bar still shows how much you have packed, but capacity is treated as unlimited.\n\nOnly applies to player-expedition quest shuttles; permit shuttles and player-owned shuttles are unchanged.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitEnabledTip: When unchecked, this mod no longer blocks anything over the headcount: even vanilla's "only N colonists" check on the loading panel is waived, right-click boarding does not count heads, and the Launch button is never greyed out for carrying too many or too few units that use a slot. The four options below stop having any effect.\n\nThe quest's own named people and items are unaffected - while those are missing, Launch stays grey.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitMechsTip: When checked, your mechanoids take up slots in the headcount like colonists do. Leave it unchecked and they can come along without using a slot (default).\n\nEither way, the number of colonists the quest requires is unchanged.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitSubhumansTip: When checked, your subhumans (the ghoul mutants) take up slots in the headcount like colonists do. Leave it unchecked and they can come along without using a slot (default).
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitSlavesTip: When checked, slaves take up slots in the headcount, as in vanilla (default). Uncheck to let them come along without using a slot.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitPrisonersTip: When checked, prisoners take up slots on the outbound trip, as in vanilla (default). Uncheck to let them come along without using a slot.\n\nOn the return trip, prisoners never use a slot, regardless of this option.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitNote: Note: the specific people and items a quest requires, and reachability, are judged exactly as in vanilla. Extra prisoners on the return trip and the death-cap on required colonists are always on; they have no separate toggles.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoLimitOffNote: (Passenger limits are off, so the four unit categories do not apply right now. Tick "Enforce the passenger limit" again and your settings below take effect as saved.)
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoNoRequiredColonists: Cannot launch: the quest requires at least {0} colonists aboard, and there are currently {1}.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoTooManyAboard: Cannot launch: the quest allows {0} units that use a passenger slot aboard, and there are currently {1}. Unload the extra units first. Mechanoids and subhumans that do not use a slot, and the quest's own passengers, are not counted.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoSendShuttleBoarding: {0} unit(s) are assigned to the shuttle but have not boarded yet: {1}. Launching now will leave them behind.
LanguageData.ShuttleCargoRequestDepartureDesc: Ask the quest to re-check the load and depart on its own terms. Once everything the quest asked for is aboard, the shuttle leaves for the destination the quest worked out; if nobody aboard can fly or hack it, the quest shows its own choice dialog.
